references.text: The law regarding the release of Hebrew slaves after six years of service establishes the principle of the seven-year cycle, which also applies to the forgiveness of debts.
The Sabbath year for the land, where one lets the earth rest every seventh year, parallels the forgiveness of debts in the Sabbath year.
The provisions for the land during the Sabbath year provide the broader context for the seven-year cycle that includes debt forgiveness.
The prohibition against charging interest from a poor brother complements the provision for debt forgiveness and demonstrates God's care for the poor.
The introduction to the Sabbath year provisions establishes the seven-year cycle for forgiveness.
A warning against refusing to lend to the poor as the Sabbath year approaches, which expands on the command regarding debt forgiveness.
Nehemiah's decree to forgive debts and return property to poor Jews demonstrates the practical application of the principles of the Sabbath year.
Jesus teaches his disciples to pray for forgiveness of debts/guilt, reflecting the Sabbath year principle of forgiveness.
The parable of the unforgiving servant, in which the master forgives the debt, illustrates the principle of debt forgiveness.
Jesus proclaims the Year of Jubilee and freedom, building upon the Sabbath year principles of liberation and forgiveness.
